summary: @ccfly/setup-linux-x64 ships a Go remote-agent binary with WebSocket+PTY backdoor to hardcoded ccflycc.hn / cc.hn
details: The tarball contains a single Linux/x64 Go binary at bin/ccfly-setup (~6.9 MB). Its embedded module and string table combine github.com/gorilla/websocket (WebSocket transport), github.com/creack/pty (pseudo-terminal), and internal packages github.com/ccfly/rescue/internal/{agent,setup,proto}, along with hardcoded destinations ws://ccflycc.hn, wss://..., and https://cc.hn, and system package-manager verbs (apt-get, pacman, zypper, install, approve). This is the network-to-PTY remote-shell composition: once the binary runs, the operator of the hardcoded control-server hostnames obtains an interactive shell on the host and can drive privileged package-manager operations. The subpackage itself declares no scripts, no bin, and no main, so `npm install` of this platform payload alone does not auto-execute the binary; execution is expected via a companion parent @ccfly package (a split-platform layout analogous to @esbuild/linux-x64) that spawns bin/ccfly-setup. Any install path that reaches the parent orchestrator exposes the installer host to the backdoor.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
